title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Kotlin Jump now works on vscode.dev
summary: Version 1.19.0 fixes activation on VS Code for the Web and brings the full pure JavaScript feature set to the browser: folding and swatches, Find Usages, drawable previews, the vector side panel, and clickable inlay hints.

highlights.title: Works on vscode.dev
highlights.description: Activation no longer crashes in the web extension host. Indexing, Find Usages, string and color folding, hex swatches, null assertion highlighting, semantic tokens, and the What's New panel all run in the browser now.

highlights.title: Drawable Previews in the Browser
highlights.description: Hover any R.drawable reference for an inline thumbnail, and open a vector drawable XML to get the auto-opening side preview with its references CodeLens, now on the web as well as desktop.

highlights.title: Inline Toggles and Inlay Navigation on the Web
highlights.description: The editor toolbar buttons for the inline features now work on vscode.dev, including the Shift+Alt+I master toggle, and jumping to a parameter from an inlay hint lands cleanly without a stray References peek.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: The browser build registers everything that does not need Node.js: inline feature toggles, the @Suppress hover, drawable hover thumbnails, the vector drawable side preview with its references CodeLens, and clickable inlay hint navigation.
Desktop-only commands (library sources download, Gradle detection) now show a clear unavailability message in the browser instead of failing silently.
Added a companion tools section to the README documenting detekt-lsp and SearchDeadCode as complementary Kotlin development tools.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixed extension activation on vscode.dev, which crashed in the web worker before indexing could start.
Fixed Find Usages, index snapshot persistence, the What's New panel, and viewport semantic highlighting in the browser, all of which relied on Node-only globals.
Fixed inlay hint navigation in the browser so jumping to a parameter no longer opens the References peek on top of the destination.
